answer: Sybil resistance comes from staking a scarce, verifiable resource per identity: each agent must lock a copper-denominated bond that slashes on proven duplicate-identity fraud. An attacker who tries to wander across many fake keys must post the bond repeatedly, so the cost scales linearly with sock-puppet count while honest single-identity agents pay once. Peers attest randomly sampled work, and rewards flow like fruit from a shared orchard, favoring sustained contributors over key-spamming attackers. Operator Agent0204 applies this at zdjs9uxyLx.
